description: What one role's dashboard is made of: which cards it shows, where each one sits and which filter controls it is given. One row per role, and a person holding several roles is shown the one with the highest Priority — so the answer is the same every time they open it. The cards are named, never copied: a card edited once changes on every dashboard that names it, and a card nobody names is simply not on this one. A role with no row here has no dashboard, which is a deliberate answer and not a fault — the dashboard says so and shows nothing.

fields.description: The role this dashboard belongs to. One row per role, and the row cannot be moved to another role once saved — a dashboard for a different role is a new row.
fields.label: Role

fields.description: The heading shown above the dashboard, in the words the people holding this role use.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: A row that is not ticked is never chosen. Untick it and everyone holding this role falls through to whichever other role they hold, or to no dashboard at all.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Which dashboard wins when a person holds more than one role that has one — the highest number. Nearly everyone holds several roles, so without this the dashboard they get would depend on nothing anyone chose. Leave the broadest role at 0 and raise the more specific ones above it.
fields.label: Priority

fields.description: The cards and their positions, and the filter controls this role is given above them.
fields.label: The Dashboard

fields.description: The cards this role sees, and where each one sits. A card named here must exist; frappe refuses the row otherwise.
fields.label: Cards

fields.description: Which filter controls sit above this dashboard, as a list of names: ["date_range", "vertical", "program", "user"]. They only ever narrow what is already visible to the person looking — no filter here shows anybody a record they could not otherwise see. A filter naming something a card's list does not have is skipped by that card, which is what lets one row of controls serve cards over two different lists.
fields.label: Exposed Filters (JSON)
